summary: Compact automaticity-and-take-up refinement: adds a note on claim friction, prefill, automatic delivery, and non-take-up; explains why floor protection can fail when relief exists mainly on paper; and threads low-friction claiming discipline through the archive while keeping the waist narrow.
major_judgments: Present LLMs are still not taxed as direct persons.

A tax can remain unjust even with a sensible base, incidence target, timing rule, and review architecture if its floor-protecting rebates, refunds, or repair payments are stranded behind high-friction claiming and low take-up.
Where the state already knows enough, automaticity, prefill, one-step confirmation, and accessible correction paths are morally preferred for protected relief.
High-friction application paths are more tolerable for negotiated privileges or exceptional carve-outs than for subsistence protection or routine return-of-overcollection.

Controller-first AI taxation is tightened again: automate and prefill ordinary relief where possible, but keep contestability, human help, and offline correction open rather than letting digital infrastructure become a hidden exclusion gate.
